headline: Apple's HomeView mounts cost extra starting at $59.95
summary: Apple's new $299 HomeView smart display requires separate mounts for wall installation, adding at least $59 to the total price.
details: Apple has officially launched its new HomeView smart home display, available in two models, both priced at $299. One model features a speaker base, while the other is designed for wall mounting. However, the wall-mounted version comes with a catch: the necessary mounts are sold separately.

Customers opting for the wall-mounted HomeView will need to purchase a mount, with prices starting at $59.95 for the "Power Mount USB-C Wall Connector." Another option, the "Power Mount AC Wired," is available for $79.95. A "Power Mount PoE Wired" is slated for release in early 2027 at $129.95.

The HomeView (Wall Mounted) requires a mount and power solution to operate, meaning it cannot be used without purchasing one of the additional accessories. Unlike the desktop model, the wall-mounted version cannot simply be placed on a surface to function, forcing users to incur the extra cost if they wish to wall-mount it.

This additional cost is detailed in the fine print on Apple's product announcement page and becomes apparent during the checkout process on Apple's webstore, where users must select a mount option or acknowledge that the "Wall Mounted" version requires one to operate.
